A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWAX research work. All 16 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D, are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original SWAX training and evaluation results, including retrieval, downstream tasks, and sampling-probability and annealing ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds results for models alternating sliding-window and full attention in Section 4.5 and Figure 9.

M1.justification: Section 4.5 extends the hybrid training approach to models alternating SWA and full-attention layers, an architecture previously discussed as background. The original SWAX/mLSTM design, stochastic window-selection rule and annealing procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The added experiment reuses existing RULER NIAH tasks at previously evaluated sequence lengths. The represented training data, code-generation and reasoning tasks, and LongBench, LongBench2 and BABILong coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 9 newly evaluates fixed-window local-global models with windows of 128 and 2048 against their stochastic-window counterpart. Existing comparison sets are retained. The newly cited Arcee model is contextual related work, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The added local-global experiment uses 1.4B models and reports accuracy averaged over NIAH single1–3, Multiquery and Multikey separately at 4k, 8k and 16k tokens. Existing SWAX/Gated DeltaNet protocols, training budgets and evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 9 adds a test of whether the window-size effect persists when global memory uses full attention instead of recurrent layers. The existing window-sensitivity, pure-SWA, sampling-probability and annealing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new experiment follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice; stochastic window sampling is a training mechanism, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Figure 9 shows short-window and stochastic local-global models outperforming the 2048-window variant, with stochastic training highest at 16k. Appendix Table 4 changes the annealed 1.4B SWAX ARC-e score from 28.71 to 68.71, matching Table 2 in both versions. Other existing results are retained.

T1.justification: The background definitions, memory-update/readout Equations 1–5 and complexity arguments are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added in the main text or appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly extends the window-size finding to local-global hybrids containing full attention and frames stochastic training more generally across hybrid architectures. The central short-window finding and stochastic-training contribution remain intact, as does the conclusion.

C2.justification: The abstract and Section 4.5 newly interpret the full-attention results as evidence that large local windows can hinder global layers across additional hybrid architectures. Existing explanations of recurrent-memory underuse, annealing tradeoffs and mixed realistic-benchmark performance remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendices retain the same implementation, learning-rate, batch-size, training-token, positional-embedding and sampling details. Beyond its architecture and evaluation scope, the added local-global experiment supplies no new implementation instructions, hardware/runtime information or code/data access.

R1.justification: v3 adds Singh et al. (2026), the Arcee Trinity Large technical report, and cites it alongside the existing OpenAI reference to motivate the relevance of local-global architectures. The earlier related-work discussion and references are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, contribution statements receive limited edits, and Section 4.5 gains an expanded heading and paragraph. Author affiliations are reformatted and the internship note is removed. The overall section and appendix structure remains stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 9 and renumbers the unchanged appendix plot as Figure 10. It realigns Figure 6 with Table 2, moves and reformats Table 3 beside the new plot, and widens/restyles appendix Tables 4–5. Existing plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: Section 4.5 and Figure 9 provide useful evidence that the window-size effect extends beyond recurrent-memory hybrids. Correcting Table 4 also resolves its ARC-e inconsistency with Table 2. These are limited gains: the broader applicability evidence covers only 1.4B models on retrieval tasks at 4k–16k tokens, while the original methods and results remain largely unchanged.
